response.reasoning:
Before buying, you asked specifically whether the boxes were in good condition and said that for retired sets that was most of what you were paying for; the answer you were given was that they had been stored in a cupboard since new and the boxes were fine, and the listing itself said the boxes were in good condition. So box condition was part of what was promised, not an incidental extra.

What arrived does not fully match that. The photograph of the shipping carton shows one upper corner crushed and split, with the crease running along the top edge, and the photograph of the set box shows damage at the corresponding corner: the top-left corner is crushed and the card is torn open there, with scuffing along the edges. The damage on the outer carton lines up with the damage on the set inside it, which points to the harm being done in transit rather than to the box having been sold already broken. The seller's account that it was in good condition when it left is therefore plausible, but so is the buyer's account that what was received is not what was described. Between two honest parties, the loss still has to fall somewhere, and it falls mainly on the side that chose the packing: a single carton marked fragile that let a corner impact reach the set box is what allowed this to happen, and the delivery record shows an ordinary journey with no sign of unusual handling.

Against that, the scale of the loss should be kept in proportion. This was four sets for two hundred, and one box is affected. The photograph shows a crushed and torn corner rather than a box that has been destroyed; the set itself appears intact and the front face and printing are undamaged, so the great majority of what was bought is unaffected. Reporting was prompt — the buyer raised it the day the parcel arrived — so there is no question of damage happening later in the buyer's hands.

A fair reflection of that is a partial refund covering roughly the loss of collector value on the one damaged box plus a share of the responsibility for packing, with the seller keeping the value of the three undamaged sets and the substantial remaining value of the fourth. Twenty-two per cent of the money being held to the buyer, the balance to the seller.

findings.statement: Before the sale the buyer asked directly about box condition and was told the sets had been stored in a cupboard since new and the boxes were fine; the listing also stated the boxes were in good condition.
The photograph of the outer shipping carton shows a crushed and split upper corner, indicating impact damage to the parcel.
The photograph of the set box shows a crushed and torn top corner in the position matching the damaged corner of the outer carton, with the front face and printing otherwise intact.
The delivery record shows an ordinary journey ending in delivery, and the buyer reported the damage the same day the parcel arrived.
The seller maintains the item was in good condition when sent and was carefully packed; only one of the four sets is said to be affected.
